rules.fallback: unfold always terminates with a legal course (it only deletes vertices, down to the two ends, and a 2-point course has no turn). rules.mechanism: SHARED PADDY-RING ARCHITECTURE (W16-W28): waterfields/seams/close.py:close_seams is the last stage that reshapes a paddy plot ring (carve_comb -> _comb_floor_and_winding -> _comb_toe_and_hem -> finish_comb -> close_seams -> _comb_dry_and_beans, which only reads rings). Lift ONE predicate module, waterfields/ring_rules.py:ring_violations(ring, ctx) -> set of rule names, where ctx carries the design cell, the grain, the supply index (carve._supply_index), the drain polyline and widths, and the field ponds/graves; each rule below is one function in it, and each gate test calls that function. Two mechanisms: (a) EVERY step of close_seams that writes a ring (_plant, _visible_parts, _absorb and all its ladder tiers, _trade, _unjog, _shed_necks, _repair_crossing_rings) refuses a candidate ring for which ring_violations is non-empty - the step is not taken; (b) a TERMINAL sweep at the end of close_seams (after _repair_crossing_rings(rounded=True)) sends any ring still violating (a carved ring no step touched) to the scrap path: _absorb into a neighbor if the union passes ring_violations, else the ground stays bare under the fan floor - the 'odd corner left unpaddied' the research describes and the Sawada review confirmed invisible in ink (pockets.py:_absorb's last branch). Rings are judged AS RECORDED (rounded to 0.1 px, raw and deduped), so the placer and the manifest see one ring. Rule function: working_width(ring) = area / longest minimum-rotated-rectangle side >= BASIN_MIN_WIDTH_FT * g/2. The floor is a calibrated degree along a continuum (not a knob); the research pass reads 'Minimum basin SIZE' for a stated width - if the record gives none, the number is labeled GUESS at the constant and in the spec's Decisions table, and the Senmaida strips ('a few feet wide') bound it from below.
rules.fallback: Scrap path: weld into the neighbor sharing the longest side (the width-making move), else bare.
rules.later_stages: None after close_seams.
rules.unit_test: A 6 ft x 80 ft basin at 0.3 cell: assert close_seams output has no ring under the width floor.
retire: none today (no finished-map test); a new placer unit test
rules.risk: medium - changes plot counts on fans with narrow seam basins (Kashikawa measured 30 under 16 ft); the threshold needs its research pass first.

The walk is along -fall, so t_up bounds t_clear from above (once the lowest rim point is upslope of the envelope's highest point, nothing can intersect): no step limit is needed.
